create.name: Plan Product Discovery
create.description: Build an evidence-driven continuous discovery cadence with clear learning goals, participants, methods, decision points, and evidence hygiene. Use when starting discovery, planning a research cycle, replacing an idea backlog with learning work, or deciding what the product team must learn before committing.
create.content:
---
name: plan-product-discovery
description: Build an evidence-driven continuous discovery cadence with clear learning goals, participants, methods, decision points, and evidence hygiene. Use when starting discovery, planning a research cycle, replacing an idea backlog with learning work, or deciding what the product team must learn before committing.
---

# Plan Product Discovery

## Contract

Plan discovery to retire meaningful uncertainty, not to produce research theater. Separate observed facts, interpretations, assumptions, and decisions. Scale the cadence to the cost and reversibility of the decision.

## Workflow

1. State the decision discovery must enable, its owner, deadline, and cost of being wrong.
2. Inventory current evidence and assumptions. Mark source, date, segment, and confidence; do not convert repetition into truth without independent support.
3. Rank uncertainties by decision impact and evidence weakness. Select the smallest set that could change the decision.
4. Match each uncertainty to a method: interviews for context and causality, observation for behavior, product data for prevalence, prototypes for comprehension or usability, and experiments for causal response.
5. Define participants and sampling. Include the relevant segment, non-users or churned users when useful, and explicit exclusion criteria.
6. Set a weekly operating loop: collect, tag, synthesize, decide, and update the evidence ledger. Name the point at which more research has diminishing value.
7. Produce a discovery backlog ordered by learning value, not stakeholder loudness.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, first search organization skills with `list-skills` and read a relevant result with `get-skill`. Use calls, transcripts, signals, documents, people, survey responses, and project evidence to seed the inventory. If unavailable, work from user-provided artifacts and say what was not searched.

## Output

Return the decision statement, evidence and assumption inventory, ranked learning questions, method and sample plan, cadence, stop conditions, and the next three discovery actions. Every action must name the uncertainty it retires.

## Quality Gate

Reject a plan that lacks a decision, mixes evidence with inference, samples only convenient users, or schedules activity without a learning-to-decision path.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [continuous-discovery](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/continuous-discovery) and [discovery-process](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/discovery-process); the latter is reference-only because of its noncommercial license.

create.name: Plan Customer Interviews
create.description: Prepare unbiased customer interviews that investigate past behavior, struggling moments, alternatives, and decision context. Use when writing an interview guide, recruiting participants, planning discovery calls, or checking whether questions lead respondents toward a preferred solution.
create.content:
---
name: plan-customer-interviews
description: Prepare unbiased customer interviews that investigate past behavior, struggling moments, alternatives, and decision context. Use when writing an interview guide, recruiting participants, planning discovery calls, or checking whether questions lead respondents toward a preferred solution.
---

# Plan Customer Interviews

## Contract

Seek concrete history before opinions. Ask about the respondent's world, not whether they like the team's idea. A good interview can disconfirm the premise.

## Workflow

1. Write the learning objective and the product decision it may change.
2. Define participant criteria from behavior, situation, or segment; distinguish users, buyers, admins, churned customers, and non-consumers.
3. Draft a short guide: context, last occurrence, sequence of events, current workaround, consequences, alternatives considered, and commitment or next step.
4. Replace leading, hypothetical, compound, and satisfaction-only questions with prompts about specific recent behavior. Ask `what happened next?`, `show me`, and `why then?`.
5. Plan consent, recording, note-taking, timeboxes, interviewer roles, and a neutral closing.
6. Define capture fields before the call: verbatim evidence, observed behavior, inference, follow-up, segment, and source ID.
7. Pilot the guide once. Remove questions that invite speeches but do not affect the decision.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use existing calls, transcripts, signals, people, CRM properties, and survey responses to avoid re-asking known questions and recruit the right evidence gaps. Do not contact or schedule anyone unless the user explicitly authorizes it.

## Output

Return the objective, participant screener, 30-45 minute guide, interviewer notes, capture schema, consent checklist, pilot changes, and synthesis handoff.

## Quality Gate

Flag every question that asks for prediction, praise, feature design, or a numeric rating without behavioral follow-up. The guide must leave room for the premise to be wrong.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [user-interview](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/user-interview), [customer-interviews](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/customer-interviews), and [interview-script](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/interview-script).

create.name: Synthesize Customer Research
create.description: Turn interviews, calls, surveys, observations, support records, and notes into traceable findings and decision implications. Use when summarizing research, comparing participants, finding themes, producing an insight brief, or separating evidence from team interpretation.
create.content:
---
name: synthesize-customer-research
description: Turn interviews, calls, surveys, observations, support records, and notes into traceable findings and decision implications. Use when summarizing research, comparing participants, finding themes, producing an insight brief, or separating evidence from team interpretation.
---

# Synthesize Customer Research

## Contract

Read the full evidence set before naming themes. Preserve the chain from source to evidence unit to pattern to insight to recommendation. Do not present a model summary as a customer quote.

## Workflow

1. Define the research question, decision, included sources, date range, segments, and exclusions.
2. Normalize atomic evidence units with source ID, speaker or respondent, date, segment, text or observation, and evidence type.
3. Tag without forcing consensus. Keep contradictory and negative cases visible.
4. Cluster by shared job, barrier, trigger, behavior, or outcome rather than vocabulary alone.
5. Write findings as claims. For each, attach supporting units, counterevidence, prevalence within the sample, and confidence.
6. Derive implications and recommendations separately. Mark which recommendations are decisions, experiments, or follow-up questions.
7. Check whether one account, researcher, source type, or prompt dominates the result.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Retrieve stable evidence pages from calls, transcripts, signals or extractions, survey responses, documents, and people. Record returned IDs and filters. Use aggregates for counts and row-level tools for representative evidence; do not infer coverage from one result page.

## Output

Return scope, method, evidence table, findings ordered by strength, counterevidence, segment differences, implications, recommendations, open questions, and a source ledger.

## Quality Gate

Every finding must be falsifiable and traceable. Downgrade confidence when evidence is sparse, old, prompted, segment-skewed, internally paraphrased, or contradicted.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [research-synthesis](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/research-synthesis), [analyzing-user-feedback](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/analyzing-user-feedback), and [summarize-interview](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/summarize-interview).

create.name: Segment Product Market
create.description: Segment a product market using evidence about jobs, situations, behavior, needs, adoption constraints, economics, and value potential. Use when mapping heterogeneous demand, comparing customer groups, choosing a beachhead, or establishing the segments an ICP decision should evaluate.
create.content:
---
name: segment-product-market
description: Segment a product market using evidence about jobs, situations, behavior, needs, adoption constraints, economics, and value potential. Use when mapping heterogeneous demand, comparing customer groups, choosing a beachhead, or establishing the segments an ICP decision should evaluate.
---

# Segment Product Market

## Contract

Segmentation explains meaningful differences in value, behavior, or buying conditions. Do not create decorative personas or clusters that cannot change product, positioning, distribution, or investment decisions.

## Workflow

1. Define the decision, market boundary, product state, geography, and evidence horizon.
2. Assemble evidence from customers, non-users, churned users, alternatives, usage, sales, support, and market sources. Label source, date, sample, and confidence.
3. Generate candidate segmentation dimensions from jobs, triggering situations, behavior, workflow, constraints, value realized, willingness to change, and buying context before demographics.
4. Test whether each candidate creates internally coherent and externally distinct groups with observable membership signals.
5. Compare segments on problem intensity, reach, urgency, ability to adopt, time to value, economics, accessibility, competitive pressure, and strategic fit.
6. Select the smallest useful segmentation model. Name overlaps, edge cases, unknown membership, and segments intentionally combined or deferred.
7. Describe implications for product experience, evidence collection, positioning, channels, pricing, success, and the subsequent ICP decision.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, signals, surveys, people and account properties, projects, and documents to compare needs and contexts. Respect access boundaries and never infer sensitive traits that were not explicitly provided.

## Output

Return decision context, evidence inventory, candidate dimensions, selected segmentation model, segment profiles, comparison matrix, membership signals, implications, confidence, and validation plan.

## Quality Gate

Reject segments defined only by convenient firmographics, unsupported stereotypes, or labels that do not lead to different decisions. Keep the market map distinct from the primary ICP selection.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [market-segments](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-market-research/skills/market-segments), [user-segmentation](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-market-research/skills/user-segmentation), and [defining-icp](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/defining-icp).

create.name: Cluster Feedback Into Jobs
create.description: Reframe a body of feature requests, complaints, call snippets, tickets, and survey responses into customer jobs with a traceable clustering receipt. Use when a feedback backlog is noisy, duplicated, solution-led, or too fragmented to support product decisions.
create.content:
---
name: cluster-feedback-into-jobs
description: Reframe a body of feature requests, complaints, call snippets, tickets, and survey responses into customer jobs with a traceable clustering receipt. Use when a feedback backlog is noisy, duplicated, solution-led, or too fragmented to support product decisions.
---

# Cluster Feedback Into Jobs

## Contract

Cluster on the progress customers seek in a situation, not on the requested feature or shared nouns. Preserve ambiguous items and the mapping back to raw evidence.

## Workflow

1. Define scope, segments, dates, sources, and the decision this clustering informs.
2. For each item, record the situation, desired progress, blocked outcome, current workaround, urgency trigger, and literal request. Leave fields unknown rather than inventing context.
3. Draft a provisional job for sufficiently rich items. Put thin or ambiguous items in an unresolved queue.
4. Cluster items whose situations and desired progress are materially alike, even when their proposed solutions differ.
5. Split clusters that contain independently shippable jobs or distinct causal barriers. Merge clusters that differ only in wording.
6. Rate each cluster on evidence volume, source diversity, severity, trend, strategic relevance, and confidence; keep these axes separate.
7. Produce a receipt mapping every item to a cluster or unresolved reason.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first, then use signals or structured extractions for the evidence set. Filter direct customer voice explicitly when required, preserve signal and call IDs, and use aggregation only for counts after the clusters are defined.

## Output

Return job clusters, job statements, evidence counts, representative evidence, workarounds, triggers, ratings, unresolved items, and the complete item-to-cluster ledger.

## Quality Gate

Reject labels such as `dashboard requests` or `export features` unless they describe the customer progress. Do not rank roadmap priority from volume alone.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [feedback-to-jobs](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/feedback-to-jobs), [jtbd-analysis](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/jtbd-analysis), and [analyze-feature-requests](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/analyze-feature-requests).

create.name: Define Jobs To Be Done
create.description: Define a durable job to be done from customer evidence, including situation, motivation, outcome, alternatives, forces, success evidence, and boundaries. Use when reframing a feature request, writing a job story, clarifying the customer outcome, or creating an outcome contract before solution design.
create.content:
---
name: define-jobs-to-be-done
description: Define a durable job to be done from customer evidence, including situation, motivation, outcome, alternatives, forces, success evidence, and boundaries. Use when reframing a feature request, writing a job story, clarifying the customer outcome, or creating an outcome contract before solution design.
---

# Define Jobs To Be Done

## Contract

Describe progress in the customer's world. Keep implementation, product names, and preferred solutions out of the job definition. Treat a draft inferred from feedback as unconfirmed until reviewed against source evidence or with the user.

## Workflow

1. Gather concrete struggling moments, current behavior, workarounds, consequences, and switching events.
2. Identify the job owner and the specific situation that creates demand.
3. Write the core job: `When [situation], I want to [progress], so I can [outcome].`
4. Map forces: push from the current state, pull toward change, anxiety about change, and habit or switching cost.
5. State functional, emotional, and social dimensions only when evidence supports them.
6. Define observable success, failure, non-goals, and the alternatives the new solution must beat.
7. Attach evidence and uncertainties. Test durability by imagining a complete rebuild: the job should remain true.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use customer signals, transcripts, survey responses, people context, and documents to ground each clause. Cite source IDs and distinguish direct voice from internal interpretation.

## Output

Return the job story, struggling moment, progress and outcome, forces, alternatives, success and failure evidence, boundaries, supporting sources, unresolved assumptions, and confirmation status.

## Quality Gate

Rewrite any job that contains a feature, channel, database, UI control, or company-specific implementation. Do not claim frequency or importance without a defined evidence set.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [create-job-spec](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/create-job-spec), [jtbd-analysis](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/jtbd-analysis), and [job-stories](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/job-stories).

create.name: Map Customer Journey
create.description: Map an evidence-backed customer journey across stages, actors, jobs, touchpoints, emotions, friction, handoffs, and measures. Use when diagnosing an end-to-end experience, finding service gaps, aligning teams around a journey, or comparing journeys across customer segments.
create.content:
---
name: map-customer-journey
description: Map an evidence-backed customer journey across stages, actors, jobs, touchpoints, emotions, friction, handoffs, and measures. Use when diagnosing an end-to-end experience, finding service gaps, aligning teams around a journey, or comparing journeys across customer segments.
---

# Map Customer Journey

## Contract

Map what customers actually do, including off-product and human steps. Keep the current-state journey separate from the desired future state. Avoid decorative maps without evidence or owners.

## Workflow

1. Define the journey's actor, segment, start trigger, end outcome, and scope boundary.
2. Gather behavioral evidence across calls, observation, product data, support, surveys, and service teams.
3. Lay out stages in customer language. For each, record job, action, touchpoint, expectation, emotion, friction, workaround, handoff, and evidence.
4. Mark moments that disproportionately affect trust, conversion, activation, retention, or cost.
5. Separate observed problems from hypothesized causes. Note segment and role differences rather than averaging incompatible journeys.
6. Prioritize opportunities by customer impact, frequency, strategic relevance, and control.
7. Assign measures and an owner to each selected opportunity; capture gaps requiring further research.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, signals, survey responses, people properties, documents, and projects to triangulate each stage. Preserve IDs and date ranges; do not treat internal descriptions as observed customer behavior.

## Output

Return scope, actor and segment, current-state journey table, key moments, evidence gaps, prioritized opportunities, measures, owners, and a clearly labeled future-state sketch when requested.

## Quality Gate

Every stage needs evidence or an explicit hypothesis label. Reject a map that starts and ends at product screens when the customer job extends beyond them.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [customer-journey-map](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-market-research/skills/customer-journey-map) and [customer-journey-map](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/customer-journey-map); the latter is reference-only because of its noncommercial license.

create.name: Analyze Competitors
create.description: Analyze direct competitors, indirect alternatives, non-consumption, and customer switching criteria using current evidence. Use when researching a market, preparing positioning, evaluating strategic threats, creating a battlecard, or avoiding a feature-only comparison.
create.content:
---
name: analyze-competitors
description: Analyze direct competitors, indirect alternatives, non-consumption, and customer switching criteria using current evidence. Use when researching a market, preparing positioning, evaluating strategic threats, creating a battlecard, or avoiding a feature-only comparison.
---

# Analyze Competitors

## Contract

Compare how customers solve the job, not only vendors that share a category. Use current primary sources for unstable claims. Distinguish verified facts, customer perceptions, and analyst inference.

## Workflow

1. Define the customer, job, decision, geography, and time horizon.
2. Enumerate alternatives: direct products, adjacent tools, internal workflows, services, spreadsheets, and doing nothing.
3. Collect comparable evidence on target customer, value claim, workflow, switching costs, proof, pricing model, distribution, and constraints.
4. Add customer evidence about why alternatives are chosen, rejected, or replaced.
5. Compare on decision criteria that matter to the target segment, not a maximal feature matrix.
6. Identify defended strengths, credible gaps, market shifts, and assumptions requiring validation.
7. Derive strategic implications: where to compete, where not to compete, and which claim needs proof.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signals, transcripts, documents, knowledge pages, and survey responses for alternative and switching evidence. Use web or supplied primary sources for current competitor facts; cite both evidence classes separately.

## Output

Return scope, alternative set, decision criteria, evidence matrix, customer switching evidence, strategic gaps, implications, watch items, and sources with dates.

## Quality Gate

Reject unsupported claims, stale pricing or product facts, false precision, and tables whose rows are irrelevant to customer choice. Never infer competitor strategy from one feature.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [competitor-analysis](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/competitor-analysis), [competitive-strategy](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/competitive-strategy), and [competitor-analysis](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-market-research/skills/competitor-analysis).

create.name: Map Product Opportunities
create.description: Build an evidence-backed opportunity map connecting a desired outcome to customer problems, possible solutions, assumptions, and tests. Use when creating an opportunity solution tree, organizing discovery, comparing solution paths, or preventing idea-first roadmapping.
create.content:
---
name: map-product-opportunities
description: Build an evidence-backed opportunity map connecting a desired outcome to customer problems, possible solutions, assumptions, and tests. Use when creating an opportunity solution tree, organizing discovery, comparing solution paths, or preventing idea-first roadmapping.
---

# Map Product Opportunities

## Contract

Keep outcomes, opportunities, solutions, and experiments at distinct levels. An opportunity describes unmet customer progress or friction, not a feature. Branches may compete; the map is a learning model, not a promise tree.

## Workflow

1. Define one measurable customer or business outcome and the relevant segment.
2. Gather source evidence and extract opportunities in customer language.
3. Group opportunities by causal relationship to the outcome. Split overlapping jobs and preserve contradictory evidence.
4. Attach evidence strength, prevalence within the searched set, severity, segment, and key assumptions to each node.
5. Generate multiple solution approaches only for the best-supported opportunities; include operational or policy changes where relevant.
6. Identify desirability, usability, feasibility, viability, and ethical or compliance assumptions for each approach.
7. Attach the cheapest decisive test to the riskiest assumption. Mark decisions and updates as evidence changes.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signals, survey responses, calls, documents, and project context for opportunities and supporting evidence. Preserve evidence IDs; use synthetic personas only as hypothesis generators, never as proof of real demand.

## Output

Return the target outcome, opportunity hierarchy, evidence and confidence per node, solution branches, assumption register, test plan, selected path, and unresolved gaps.

## Quality Gate

Every opportunity must be customer-centered, evidence-linked, mutually intelligible, and plausibly causal to the outcome. Remove duplicate feature-shaped nodes.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [opportunity-mapping](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/opportunity-mapping) and [opportunity-solution-tree](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/opportunity-solution-tree).
